'''Tao Zhang''' ({{zh|c=张涛}}) is a Chinese chemist and [[Academician]] of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] (CAS), working in [[heterogeneous catalysis]]. He is a professor at the [[Dalian Institute of Chemical Physics]] (DICP), which he directed from 2007 to 2016, and served as a Vice President of CAS from 2016 to 2023. He is known for introducing the concept of ''single-atom catalysis'' and for work on the catalytic conversion of cellulose to ethylene glycol.<ref name="dicp" />

== Education ==
Zhang received a B.S. in chemistry from Shaanxi University of Technology (1978–1982). He then studied catalysis at DICP, earning an M.S. (1983–1986) and a Ph.D. (1986–1989). From 1989 to 1990 he was a postdoctoral researcher at the School of Chemistry, [[University of Birmingham]], United Kingdom.<ref name="dicp" />

== Career ==
Zhang joined the faculty of DICP as an assistant professor in 1990, became associate professor in 1992 and full professor in October 1995. He was deputy director of DICP from 1998 to 2007 and director from February 2007 to December 2016. From December 2016 to September 2023 he was a Vice President of the Chinese Academy of Sciences.<ref name="dicp" />

He is Editor-in-Chief of the ''[[Chinese Journal of Catalysis]]'' and an Associate Editor of the ''[[Journal of the American Chemical Society]]''. He is co-chair of the editorial advisory board of ''[[Chemistry – A European Journal]]'' and sits on the editorial boards of ''[[Applied Catalysis B]]'', ''[[Green Chemistry (journal)|Green Chemistry]]'', ''[[ACS Sustainable Chemistry & Engineering]]'', ''[[ChemPhysChem]]'' and ''[[Industrial & Engineering Chemistry Research]]''.<ref name="dicp" />

== Research ==
=== Single-atom catalysis ===
Zhang and co-workers reported a platinum catalyst in which isolated Pt atoms are anchored on iron oxide (Pt<sub>1</sub>/FeO<sub>x</sub>) and showed activity for CO oxidation and preferential oxidation of CO; the work introduced the term "single-atom catalysis".<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Qiao |first1=Botao |last2=Wang |first2=Aiqin |last3=Yang |first3=Xiaofeng |last4=Allard |first4=Lawrence F. |last5=Jiang |first5=Zheng |last6=Cui |first6=Yitao |last7=Liu |first7=Jingyue |last8=Li |first8=Jun |last9=Zhang |first9=Tao |title=Single-atom catalysis of CO oxidation using Pt<sub>1</sub>/FeO<sub>x</sub> |journal=Nature Chemistry |year=2011 |volume=3 |issue=8 |pages=634–641 |doi=10.1038/nchem.1095}}</ref> Single-atom catalysts aim for atomically defined active sites and maximal use of precious metals, and the area has since become an active field in heterogeneous catalysis, studied by many research groups worldwide.{{citation needed|date=November 2026}}

=== Cellulose to ethylene glycol ===
Zhang's group reported the catalytic conversion of cellulose to ethylene glycol over tungsten carbide-based catalysts, a route to a bulk chemical from biomass.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Ji |first1=Na |last2=Zhang |first2=Tao |last3=Zheng |first3=Mingyuan |last4=Wang |first4=Aiqin |last5=Wang |first5=Hua |last6=Wang |first6=Xiaodong |last7=Chen |first7=Jingguang G. |title=Direct catalytic conversion of cellulose into ethylene glycol using nickel-promoted tungsten carbide catalysts |journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition |year=2008 |volume=47 |issue=44 |pages=8510–8513 |doi=10.1002/anie.200803233}}</ref>
